[March 2017]

Conservative [Chancellor of the Exchequer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_of_the_Exchequer), George Osborne, reports that her Majesty's Treasury's £716 billion ($1.18 trillion) of revenue in 2016 is expected to rise this year to £720 billion ($1.03 trillion), while the conservative parliamentarian majority has managed to cut a lot of wasteful spending, bringing 2016's £772 billion ($1.27 trillion) in expenditures down to a projected £702b ($1.01 trillion).

Mr. Osborne was elated to deliver the news:

> This the first budget surplus in a bloody long while, and those Labour wankers shouldn't share in the spoils of it. I swear to high heaven, if I hear that any of my surplus is used toward welfare or ivory tower university subsidization, I'll move to the US and vote for Donald Trump.

When told that the American election had already happened, and that Hillary Clinton had won, Mr. Osborne murmured something about moving to Peru and joining a guerrilla fighting force instead.

Although the penny-pinching Parliament would like to pay down foreign debt principal with this £18 billion ($25b), the balance is expected to be spent on new offshore projects outside of Suffolk, near the platform now known as Sealand.

One such line item for 5-year budget planning is $50m for a 1,000 bed prison platform. When asked how the Exchequer came to this amount, he merely stated that:

> "Sealand gave us [some numbers](https://voat.co/v/ModernPowers/comments/991854/4970165), and we estimated a bit lower to account for the fact that we won't have to build, staff, or insure it like a normal supermax prison, because it's in the middle of the bollacking ocean."

Since this platform would house mainly UK prisoners, and their relocation would in effect shutter expensive operations in mainland UK, the Exchequer will actually see a net profit in the long term. The initial construction of these facilities will be the brunt of the expense.

Other line items show investment in a heavy industry/alternative energy platform, as well as a waste incineration platform to help avoid dumping any more rubbish on Wales. The prices for these have yet to be determined.

In other news, it is still not clear whether Parliament is willing to spend any of this surplus on that ginger twat being held somewhere in Siberia. One MP was quoted as saying that:

> "...the amount of money Timothy Peake wasted bringing [gorilla costumes, rugby balls and fake tuxedos](http://www.dailymail.co.uk/sciencetech/article-3465356/Gorilla-costumes-rugby-balls-fake-tuxedos-Astronauts-spend-63-000-funding-sending-novelty-items-ISS.html) into space is a sign that he might not be welcome in Britain's new budgetary environment. There is no room for horseplay here, no room for error in judgement."

At press time, Angela Peake was coming to her senses that her son might not be a national hero, after all.
